claim: Zebrafish banp mutant rw337 has smaller eyes at 4 days post-fertilization (dpf).
source: rw337 mutants have smaller eyes and a smaller optic tectum at 4 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Directly stated in text and shown in Figure 1A comparing wild-type and rw337 mutant embryos.

claim: Zebrafish banp mutant rw337 has a smaller optic tectum at 4 dpf.
source: rw337 mutants have smaller eyes and a smaller optic tectum at 4 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Directly stated in text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Zebrafish banp mutant rw337 dies around 6-7 dpf.
source: Around 6–7 dpf, rw337 mutants die, indicating that this mutation is lethal.
evidence: Directly observed and stated in the manuscript.

claim: The rw337 mutation is lethal.
source: Around 6–7 dpf, rw337 mutants die, indicating that this mutation is lethal.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that mutants die at 6-7 dpf.

claim: At 1.5 dpf, there is no difference in retinal morphology between rw337 mutants and wild-type siblings.
source: At 1.5 dpf, the retina consists of retinal progenitor cells and early differentiating neurons. There was no difference in retinal morphology between rw337 mutants and wild-type siblings.
evidence: Directly stated based on histological examination.

claim: At 2 dpf, mitotic-like round cells accumulate in the apical region of the retina in rw337 mutants.
source: However, at 2 dpf, mitotic-like round cells had accumulated in the apical region of the retina in rw337 mutants, suggesting mitotic arrest or prolonged duration of mitosis.
evidence: Directly observed in histological sections shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mitotic-like round cell accumulation in rw337 mutants at 2 dpf suggests mitotic arrest or prolonged duration of mitosis.
source: However, at 2 dpf, mitotic-like round cells had accumulated in the apical region of the retina in rw337 mutants, suggesting mitotic arrest or prolonged duration of mitosis.
evidence: Inference based on the observation of accumulated mitotic-like cells.

claim: At 2.5 dpf, wild-type retinas have formed three nuclear layers (RGC layer, INL, and ONL) and two plexiform layers (IPL and OPL).
source: At 2.5 dpf, in wild-type retinas, three nuclear layers, the RGC layer, the inner nuclear layer (INL) and the outer nuclear layer (ONL), and two plexiform layers, the inner plexiform layer (IPL) and the outer plexiform layer (OPL), had formed.
evidence: Directly stated based on histological examination.

claim: At 2.5 dpf, rw337 mutants show only the RGC layer with many pyknotic nuclei in the outer retinal region.
source: In rw337 mutants, only the RGC layer was observed; however, many pyknotic nuclei were observed in the outer retinal region.
evidence: Directly observed in histological sections.

claim: At 3 dpf, rw337 mutants show RGC layer, IPL and INL, but pyknotic nuclei are densely packed in the outer region.
source: At 3 dpf, the RGC layer, IPL and INL appeared in rw337 mutants. However, pyknotic nuclei were densely packed in the outer region of rw337 mutant retinas.
evidence: Directly observed in histological sections.

claim: At 4 dpf, most dead cell debris has decreased in rw337 mutants.
source: At 4 dpf, most dead cell debris had decreased in rw337 mutants.
evidence: Directly observed in histological sections.

claim: At 4 dpf, rw337 mutants have formed RGC layer, IPL, and INL, but no ONL is observed.
source: The RGC layer, IPL, and INL were formed; however, no ONL was observed, despite very small, patchy photoreceptor-like cells.
evidence: Directly observed in histological sections.

claim: At 3 and 4 dpf, the ciliary marginal zone (CMZ) is observed in rw337 mutants.
source: At 3 and 4 dpf, the ciliary marginal zone (CMZ), where retinal stem and progenitor cells are located, was observed in rw337 mutants.
evidence: Directly observed in histological sections.

claim: RGCs differentiate in rw337 mutants.
source: Thus, RGCs differentiate, but cell death occurs after 2.5 dpf in rw337 mutants.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of RGC layer in mutant retinas.

claim: Cell death occurs after 2.5 dpf in rw337 mutants.
source: Thus, RGCs differentiate, but cell death occurs after 2.5 dpf in rw337 mutants.
evidence: Directly observed through pyknotic nuclei and TUNEL staining.

claim: The rw337 mutation is mapped to zebrafish chromosome 25.
source: We mapped the rw337 mutation to zebrafish chromosome 25 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Directly stated based on genetic mapping experiments.

claim: The genomic region containing the rw337 mutation is flanked by polymorphic markers 070702B and zC93F2D.
source: Two polymorphic markers, 070702B and zC93F2D, restricted the genomic region encompassing rw337 mutation, in which only four candidate genes: BTG3-associated nuclear protein (banp); programmed cell death 2-like (pdcd2l); carboxylesterase 2b (ces2b); protein disulfide isomerase family A, member 3 (pdia3), were annotated.
evidence: Directly stated based on genetic mapping.

claim: Four candidate genes are located in the genomic region containing the rw337 mutation: banp, pdcd2l, ces2b, and pdia3.
source: Two polymorphic markers, 070702B and zC93F2D, restricted the genomic region encompassing rw337 mutation, in which only four candidate genes: BTG3-associated nuclear protein (banp); programmed cell death 2-like (pdcd2l); carboxylesterase 2b (ces2b); protein disulfide isomerase family A, member 3 (pdia3), were annotated.
evidence: Directly stated based on genome annotation.

claim: In rw337 mutants, part of the intron sequence between exons 4 and 5 of banp fails to be spliced out.
source: We cloned all these cDNAs from mRNA prepared from rw337 homozygous mutants, sequenced them, and found that part of the intron sequence between exons 4 and 5 (intron 4/5) failed to be spliced out of the banp cDNA (Figure 1D).
evidence: Directly observed through cDNA sequencing.

claim: In rw337 mutants, nucleotide T at the exon-intron junction of exon 4 is converted to G in the banp gene.
source: A nucleotide T at the exon-intron junction of exon 4 is converted to G, which alters the donor splice site of exon 4 from GT to GG.
evidence: Directly observed through DNA sequencing.

claim: The T to G conversion at the exon-intron junction alters the donor splice site of exon 4 from GT to GG in rw337 mutants.
source: A nucleotide T at the exon-intron junction of exon 4 is converted to G, which alters the donor splice site of exon 4 from GT to GG.
evidence: Directly stated based on sequence analysis.

claim: The splice site mutation in rw337 leads to abnormal insertion of a 52 bp intron sequence after exon 4 in banp cDNA.
source: This mutation leads to abnormal insertion of a 52 bp intron sequence after exon 4, resulting in a premature stop codon in banp cDNA (Figure 1D).
evidence: Directly observed through cDNA sequencing.

claim: The 52 bp insertion in banp cDNA results in a premature stop codon in rw337 mutants.
source: This mutation leads to abnormal insertion of a 52 bp intron sequence after exon 4, resulting in a premature stop codon in banp cDNA (Figure 1D).
evidence: Directly stated based on sequence analysis.

claim: Wild-type zebrafish Banp protein contains a coiled-coil domain, a BEN domain, and a DNA-binding domain.
source: The banp gene encodes a protein containing a coiled-coil domain, a BEN domain, which was identified as a novel domain found in chromatin associated factors and DNA viral proteins and proposed to mediate protein-DNA and protein-protein interactions during chromatin organization and transcription (Abhiman et al., 2008), and a DNA-binding domain, which includes a MAR-binding domain (Figure 1E).
evidence: Directly stated based on protein domain analysis and cited literature.

claim: The BEN domain mediates protein-DNA and protein-protein interactions during chromatin organization and transcription.
source: The banp gene encodes a protein containing a coiled-coil domain, a BEN domain, which was identified as a novel domain found in chromatin associated factors and DNA viral proteins and proposed to mediate protein-DNA and protein-protein interactions during chromatin organization and transcription (Abhiman et al., 2008), and a DNA-binding domain, which includes a MAR-binding domain (Figure 1E).
evidence: Cited from Abhiman et al., 2008.

claim: The DNA-binding domain of Banp includes a MAR-binding domain.
source: The banp gene encodes a protein containing a coiled-coil domain, a BEN domain, which was identified as a novel domain found in chromatin associated factors and DNA viral proteins and proposed to mediate protein-DNA and protein-protein interactions during chromatin organization and transcription (Abhiman et al., 2008), and a DNA-binding domain, which includes a MAR-binding domain (Figure 1E).
evidence: Directly stated based on protein domain analysis.

claim: Zebrafish Banp protein shows high similarity to human and mouse Banp proteins, especially in the BEN domain.
source: Overall, zebrafish Banp protein shows high similarity to those of humans and mice, especially in the BEN domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Directly stated based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The rw337 mutation is predicted to generate nonfunctional, truncated Banp protein missing BEN and DNA-binding domains.
source: This mutation is predicted to generate nonfunctional, truncated Banp protein in rw337 mutants (Figure 1E).
evidence: Inferred from the premature stop codon location.

claim: Homozygous banpsa12976 mutant embryos phenocopy rw337 mutants.
source: Homozygous banpsa12976 mutant embryos and trans-heterozygous banprw337; banpsa12976 mutants phenocopied rw337 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Directly observed through phenotypic analysis.

claim: Trans-heterozygous banprw337; banpsa12976 mutants phenocopy rw337 mutants.
source: Homozygous banpsa12976 mutant embryos and trans-heterozygous banprw337; banpsa12976 mutants phenocopied rw337 mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Directly observed through phenotypic analysis.

claim: banp morpholino (banp MO) inhibits translation of mRNA encoding wild-type Banp.
source: We confirmed MO specificity, because banp MO inhibited translation of mRNA encoding C-terminal EGFP-tagged wild-type Banp (banp(wt)-EGFP), whereas the control, 5-mismatch banp MO (banp 5misMO) did not (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: Directly observed through fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Control 5-mismatch banp MO (banp 5misMO) does not inhibit translation of mRNA encoding wild-type Banp.
source: We confirmed MO specificity, because banp MO inhibited translation of mRNA encoding C-terminal EGFP-tagged wild-type Banp (banp(wt)-EGFP), whereas the control, 5-mismatch banp MO (banp 5misMO) did not (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: Directly observed through fluorescence microscopy.

claim: banp morphants phenocopy rw337 mutants.
source: banp morphants phenocopied rw337 mutants (Figure 1F).
evidence: Directly observed through histological analysis.

claim: Banp(wt)-EGFP protein is localized in the nuclei during interphase in developing retinas.
source: In developing retinas, Banp(wt)-EGFP protein was localized in the nuclei during interphase, whereas it spread into the whole cell region during mitosis (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and D), confirming nuclear localization of zebrafish Banp.
evidence: Directly observed through live imaging.

claim: Banp(wt)-EGFP protein spreads into the whole cell region during mitosis.
source: In developing retinas, Banp(wt)-EGFP protein was localized in the nuclei during interphase, whereas it spread into the whole cell region during mitosis (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and D), confirming nuclear localization of zebrafish Banp.
evidence: Directly observed through live imaging.

claim: EGFP-Banp(rw337) is not stably maintained in wild-type retinas.
source: We expressed Banp(wt)-EGFP, N-terminal EGFP tagged wild-type (EGFP-Banp(wt)) and the rw337 mutant form of Banp (EGFP-Banp(rw337)) in wild-type retinas. Only EGFP-Banp(rw337) was not stably maintained (Figure 1—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: Directly observed through fluorescence microscopy.

claim: EGFP-Banp(rw337) is degraded, probably by the nonsense mutation decay mechanism.
source: However, EGFP-Banp(rw337) is unstable and not maintained, suggesting that EGFP-Banp(rw337) is degraded, probably by the nonsense mutation decay mechanism.
evidence: Inferred from the instability of the truncated protein.

claim: Overexpression of Banp(wt)-EGFP rescues retinal phenotypes in rw337 mutants at 2 dpf.
source: Finally, overexpression of Banp(wt)-EGFP rescued retinal phenotypes in rw337 mutants at 2 dpf, but overexpression of EGFP-Banp(rw337) did not (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Directly observed through histological analysis and AO staining.

claim: Overexpression of EGFP-Banp(rw337) does not rescue retinal phenotypes in rw337 mutants.
source: Finally, overexpression of Banp(wt)-EGFP rescued retinal phenotypes in rw337 mutants at 2 dpf, but overexpression of EGFP-Banp(rw337) did not (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Directly observed through histological analysis and AO staining.

claim: Retinal phenotypes of rw337 mutants are caused by the loss of Banp.
source: Taken together, retinal phenotypes of rw337 mutants are caused by the loss of Banp.
evidence: Inferred from genetic mapping, sequencing, morpholino knockdown, and rescue experiments.

claim: banp mRNA shows ubiquitous expression from the one-cell stage to the 21-somite stage.
source: banp mRNA shows ubiquitous expression from the one-cell stage to the 21-somite stage, suggesting maternal and zygotic expression.
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: banp mRNA expression suggests maternal and zygotic expression.
source: banp mRNA shows ubiquitous expression from the one-cell stage to the 21-somite stage, suggesting maternal and zygotic expression.
evidence: Inferred from the early expression pattern.

claim: banp mRNA is restricted to the brain, including the retina at 30 and 48 hpf.
source: mRNA was restricted to the brain, including the retina at 30 and 48 hpf.
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: banp mRNA is expressed in neural retina at 24 hpf.
source: Frontal sections show that mRNA is expressed in neural retina at 24 hpf, but restricted in the CMZ at 48 hpf, suggesting that retinal progenitor cells express banp mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization on sections.

claim: banp mRNA is restricted to the CMZ at 48 hpf.
source: Frontal sections show that mRNA is expressed in neural retina at 24 hpf, but restricted in the CMZ at 48 hpf, suggesting that retinal progenitor cells express banp mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization on sections.

claim: Retinal progenitor cells express banp mRNA.
source: Frontal sections show that mRNA is expressed in neural retina at 24 hpf, but restricted in the CMZ at 48 hpf, suggesting that retinal progenitor cells express banp mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: Inferred from the expression pattern in neural retina and CMZ.

claim: banp mRNA expression is observed in fin and notochord at 48 hpf.
source: In addition to brain and retina, banp mRNA expression was observed in fin and notochord at 48 hpf and in neuromasts of the lateral line after 72 hpf.
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: banp mRNA expression is observed in neuromasts of the lateral line after 72 hpf.
source: In addition to brain and retina, banp mRNA expression was observed in fin and notochord at 48 hpf and in neuromasts of the lateral line after 72 hpf.
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: banp mRNA expression is not detected in banprw337 homozygous mutants at 3 dpf.
source: banp mRNA expression was not detected in banprw337 homozygous mutants at 3 dpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 6C), suggesting mRNA decay.
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: The absence of banp mRNA in banprw337 mutants suggests mRNA decay.
source: banp mRNA expression was not detected in banprw337 homozygous mutants at 3 dpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 6C), suggesting mRNA decay.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of mRNA signal.

claim: banp mRNA is prominently expressed in developing brain in zebrafish.
source: Thus, banp mRNA is prominently expressed in developing brain in zebrafish.
evidence: Summarized from in situ hybridization data.

claim: TUNEL-positive cells are rarely observed in wild-type retinas from 29 to 101 hpf.
source: TUNEL+ cells were rarely observed in wild-type retinas throughout stages from 29 to 101 hpf, as well as in banprw337mutant retinas at 24 hpf (Figure 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining.

claim: TUNEL-positive cells are rarely observed in banprw337 mutant retinas at 24 hpf.
source: TUNEL+ cells were rarely observed in wild-type retinas throughout stages from 29 to 101 hpf, as well as in banprw337mutant retinas at 24 hpf (Figure 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining.

claim: TUNEL-positive cells appear in the neural retina of banprw337 mutants at 53 hpf.
source: However, in banprw337mutants, TUNEL+ cells appeared in the neural retina at 53 hpf, and became more localized to the outer retina at 77hpf (Figure 2B) and to the interface between the central retina and the CMZ at 77 and 101 hpf (Figure 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining.

claim: TUNEL-positive cells become more localized to the outer retina at 77 hpf in banprw337 mutants.
source: However, in banprw337mutants, TUNEL+ cells appeared in the neural retina at 53 hpf, and became more localized to the outer retina at 77hpf (Figure 2B) and to the interface between the central retina and the CMZ at 77 and 101 hpf (Figure 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining.

claim: TUNEL-positive cells localize to the interface between the central retina and the CMZ at 77 and 101 hpf in banprw337 mutants.
source: However, in banprw337mutants, TUNEL+ cells appeared in the neural retina at 53 hpf, and became more localized to the outer retina at 77hpf (Figure 2B) and to the interface between the central retina and the CMZ at 77 and 101 hpf (Figure 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining.

claim: After 53 hpf, the number of TUNEL-positive cells is significantly higher in banprw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings.
source: After 53 hpf, the number of TUNEL+ cells was significantly higher in banp rw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings (Figure 2C).
evidence: Directly quantified from TUNEL staining data.

claim: Retinal cells undergo apoptosis in banprw337 mutants.
source: Thus, retinal cells undergo apoptosis in banprw337mutants.
evidence: Inferred from TUNEL staining results.

claim: The number of pH3-positive cells does not differ between wild-type and banprw337 mutant retinas at 24 hpf.
source: The number of pH3+ cells did not differ between wild-type and banprw337mutant retinas at 24 hpf.
evidence: Directly quantified from pH3 antibody staining.

claim: pH3-positive cells are markedly increased and located at the apical surface of the neural retina in banprw337 mutant retinas at 53 hpf.
source: However, pH3+ cells were markedly increased and located at the apical surface of the neural retina in banprw337mutant retinas at 53 hpf (Figure 2B'), confirming mitotic cell accumulation.
evidence: Directly observed through pH3 antibody staining.

claim: At 77 and 101 hpf, pH3-positive cells disappear from the central retina but are still accumulated in the CMZ in banprw337 mutants.
source: At 77 and 101 hpf, pH3+ cells disappeared from the central retina, but still were accumulated in the CMZ in banprw337 mutants (Figure 2B').
evidence: Directly observed through pH3 antibody staining.

claim: The number of pH3-positive cells in banprw337 mutant retinas increases transiently at 53 hpf.
source: The number of pH3+ cells in banprw337 mutant retinas increased transiently at 53 hpf, and then decreased, but was still significantly higher than that of wild-type sibling retinas after 77 hpf because of accumulation of pH3+ cells at the CMZ (Figure 2D).
evidence: Directly quantified from pH3 antibody staining.

claim: After 77 hpf, the number of pH3-positive cells is still significantly higher in banprw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings due to accumulation at the CMZ.
source: The number of pH3+ cells in banprw337 mutant retinas increased transiently at 53 hpf, and then decreased, but was still significantly higher than that of wild-type sibling retinas after 77 hpf because of accumulation of pH3+ cells at the CMZ (Figure 2D).
evidence: Directly quantified from pH3 antibody staining.

claim: There is no significant difference in BrdU-positive area between wild-type and banprw337 mutant retinas at 48 hpf.
source: The percentage of BrdU+ area to total retinal area did not differ significantly between wild-type siblings and banprw337 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), whereas the percentage of ath5:EGFP+ area to the total retinal area was slightly, but significantly lower in banprw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that retinal neurogenesis is slightly reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf, probably due to mitotic defects or apoptosis.
evidence: Directly quantified from BrdU incorporation assay.

claim: The percentage of ath5:EGFP-positive area is slightly but significantly lower in banprw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings at 48 hpf.
source: The percentage of BrdU+ area to total retinal area did not differ significantly between wild-type siblings and banprw337 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), whereas the percentage of ath5:EGFP+ area to the total retinal area was slightly, but significantly lower in banprw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that retinal neurogenesis is slightly reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf, probably due to mitotic defects or apoptosis.
evidence: Directly quantified from ath5:EGFP expression.

claim: Retinal neurogenesis is slightly reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf, probably due to mitotic defects or apoptosis.
source: The percentage of BrdU+ area to total retinal area did not differ significantly between wild-type siblings and banprw337 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), whereas the percentage of ath5:EGFP+ area to the total retinal area was slightly, but significantly lower in banprw337 mutants than in wild-type siblings (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that retinal neurogenesis is slightly reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf, probably due to mitotic defects or apoptosis.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced ath5:EGFP expression.

claim: Both caspase 3-positive and pH3-positive cells are increased in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: Both caspase 3+ and pH3+ cells were increased in banprw337 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Directly quantified from antibody staining.

claim: Caspase 3-positive cells are mostly located in the intermediate zone of the neural retina along the apico-basal axis in banprw337 mutants.
source: Furthermore, caspase 3+ cells were mostly located in the intermediate zone of the neural retina along the apico-basal axis, whereas pH3+ cells were localized at the apical surface of the neural retina (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that apoptosis occurs mostly in retinal progenitor cells undergoing G1, S, or G2 phase, or differentiating neurons.
evidence: Directly observed through spatial analysis of antibody staining.

claim: pH3-positive cells are localized at the apical surface of the neural retina in banprw337 mutants.
source: Furthermore, caspase 3+ cells were mostly located in the intermediate zone of the neural retina along the apico-basal axis, whereas pH3+ cells were localized at the apical surface of the neural retina (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that apoptosis occurs mostly in retinal progenitor cells undergoing G1, S, or G2 phase, or differentiating neurons.
evidence: Directly observed through spatial analysis of antibody staining.

claim: Apoptosis occurs mostly in retinal progenitor cells undergoing G1, S, or G2 phase, or differentiating neurons in banprw337 mutants.
source: Furthermore, caspase 3+ cells were mostly located in the intermediate zone of the neural retina along the apico-basal axis, whereas pH3+ cells were localized at the apical surface of the neural retina (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that apoptosis occurs mostly in retinal progenitor cells undergoing G1, S, or G2 phase, or differentiating neurons.
evidence: Inferred from the spatial distribution of caspase 3-positive cells.

claim: The percentage of ath5:EGFP- and caspase 3-double-positive cells to total caspase 3-positive cells is 9.44% ± 13.1% in banp mutants at 48 hpf.
source: The percentage of ath5:EGFP- and caspase 3-double-positive cells to the total number of caspase 3+ cells was 9.44% ± 13.1% in banp mutants at 48 hpf and higher than that of wild-type siblings (0.00% ± 0.00%), although the difference was not significant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: Directly quantified from double labeling experiments.

claim: The fraction of caspase 3- and HuC/D-double-positive cells among total caspase 3-positive cells is almost zero in both wild-type and banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: The fraction of caspase 3- and HuC/D-double-positive cells among total caspase 3+ cells was almost zero in both wild-type and banprw337 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K), suggesting that apoptosis does not occur in maturing retinal neurons.
evidence: Directly quantified from double labeling experiments.

claim: Apoptosis does not occur in maturing retinal neurons in banprw337 mutants.
source: The fraction of caspase 3- and HuC/D-double-positive cells among total caspase 3+ cells was almost zero in both wild-type and banprw337 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K), suggesting that apoptosis does not occur in maturing retinal neurons.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of double-positive cells.

claim: In banprw337 mutants, retinal progenitor cells primarily show mitotic defects at 48 hpf.
source: Taken together, in banprw337 mutants, retinal progenitor cells primarily show mitotic defects at 48 hpf.
evidence: Summarized from pH3 staining and live imaging data.

claim: Apoptosis is likely induced in retinal progenitor cells at interphase or in newly differentiating retinal neurons in banprw337 mutants.
source: On the other hand, apoptosis is likely induced in retinal progenitor cells at interphase or in newly differentiating retinal neurons, although apoptosis in newly differentiating retinal neurons is minor (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L).
evidence: Inferred from spatial distribution of apoptotic cells and double labeling experiments.

claim: Mitotic cell accumulation in banprw337 mutants seems to be caused by prolonged mitosis rather than permanent mitotic arrest.
source: Since mitotic cell accumulation was transiently observed in the central retina at 53 hpf (Figure 2B'), and apoptosis was not overlapped with this mitotic cell accumulation area (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), it is less likely that mitotic cells undergo permanent mitotic arrest leading to apoptosis. Rather, mitotic cell accumulation seems to be caused by prolonged mitosis.
evidence: Inferred from the transient nature of mitotic accumulation and lack of overlap with apoptosis.

claim: 258 genes are upregulated in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: 27,771 protein-coding genes were detected. Among them, 258 genes were upregulated, and 81 genes were downregulated in banprw337 mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: Directly determined from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 81 genes are downregulated in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: 27,771 protein-coding genes were detected. Among them, 258 genes were upregulated, and 81 genes were downregulated in banprw337 mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: Directly determined from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: The top 15 upregulated genes in banprw337 mutants contain a significant fraction of tp53-dependent DNA damage response regulators.
source: The top 15 upregulated genes contained a significant fraction of tp53 dependent-DNA damage response regulators (Figure 3B).
evidence: Directly observed from RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Four tp53 target genes (p21/cdkn1a, puma/bbc3, ccng1, and mdm2) are significantly upregulated in banprw337 mutants.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR revealed that four tp53 target genes: p21(cdkn1a), puma (bbc3), ccng1, and mdm2 are significantly upregulated in banprw337 mutants (Figure 3C).
evidence: Directly validated by quantitative RT-PCR.

claim: Full length tp53 protein is stabilized and more than 11-fold higher in banprw337 mutants than in wild type at 48 hpf.
source: Western blotting showed that full length tp53 (FL tp53) protein is stabilized and more than 11-fold higher in banprw337 mutants than in wild type (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Directly quantified by Western blotting.

claim: The ATR/ATM-Chk2-tp53 DNA damage pathway induces retinal apoptosis in zebrafish.
source: We previously showed that the ATR/ATM-Chk2-tp53 DNA damage pathway induces retinal apoptosis in zebrafish (Yamaguchi et al., 2008).
evidence: Cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: exo5 is a critical regulator for ATR-dependent replication fork restart.
source: Indeed, the top 15 upregulated genes contain exo5, a critical regulator for ATR-dependent replication fork restart (Hambarde et al., 2021; Figure 3B).
evidence: Cited from Hambarde et al., 2021.

claim: mRNA expression of ATR and ATM is upregulated in banprw337 mutants.
source: mRNA expression of ATR and ATM was upregulated in banprw337 mutants (Figure 3F).
evidence: Directly validated by quantitative RT-PCR.

claim: Injection of tp53 antisense morpholino completely inhibits retinal apoptosis in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: Injection of tp53 antisense morpholino (tp53 MO) completely inhibited retinal apoptosis in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining after morpholino injection.

claim: Retinal apoptosis reappears in tp53 MO-injected banprw337 mutants at 72 hpf.
source: However, retinal apoptosis reappeared in those tp53 MO-injected banprw337 mutants at 72 hpf (Figure 3G), although there was no statistical difference in apoptotic cell number between wild-type and banprw337 mutant retinas at 72 hpf (Figure 3H).
evidence: Directly observed through TUNEL staining.

claim: Retinal apoptosis in banprw337 mutants depends on tp53.
source: Thus, retinal apoptosis in banprw337 mutants depends on tp53, although it is possible that some tp53-independent mechanism induces retinal apoptosis after 48 hpf.
evidence: Inferred from tp53 MO rescue experiments.

claim: Some tp53-independent mechanism may induce retinal apoptosis after 48 hpf in banprw337 mutants.
source: Thus, retinal apoptosis in banprw337 mutants depends on tp53, although it is possible that some tp53-independent mechanism induces retinal apoptosis after 48 hpf.
evidence: Speculated based on the reappearance of apoptosis at 72 hpf despite tp53 knockdown.

claim: The mRNA level of FL tp53 is not significantly different between banprw337 mutants and wild-type siblings at 48 hpf.
source: RNA-seq analysis showed upregulation of tp53 mRNA (Figure 3B); however, surprisingly, quantitative RT-PCR showed that the mRNA level of FL tp53 is not significantly different between banprw337 mutants and wild-type siblings at 48 hpf (Figure 4A).
evidence: Directly measured by quantitative RT-PCR.

claim: In zebrafish, the isoform ∆113tp53 is generated from an alternative transcription start site in intron 4.
source: Importantly, in zebrafish, the isoform ∆113tp53 is generated from the alternative transcription start site in intron 4.
evidence: Established knowledge about zebrafish tp53 isoforms.

claim: FL tp53 initially activates transcription of ∆113tp53 after tp53 protein is stabilized in response to cellular stress.
source: It was reported that FL tp53 initially activates transcription of ∆113tp53 after tp53 protein is stabilized in response to cellular stress (Chen et al., 2009).
evidence: Cited from Chen et al., 2009.

claim: ∆113tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target genes related to cell-cycle arrest to promote DNA repair and cell survival.
source: ∆113tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target genes related to cell-cycle arrest to promote DNA repair and cell survival, whereas FL tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target apoptotic genes to eliminate severely DNA-damaged cells (Gong et al., 2015; Gong et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from Gong et al., 2015 and Gong et al., 2020.

claim: FL tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target apoptotic genes to eliminate severely DNA-damaged cells.
source: ∆113tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target genes related to cell-cycle arrest to promote DNA repair and cell survival, whereas FL tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target apoptotic genes to eliminate severely DNA-damaged cells (Gong et al., 2015; Gong et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from Gong et al., 2015 and Gong et al., 2020.

claim: Only ∆113tp53 mRNA is upregulated in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: Indeed, quantitative RT-PCR confirmed that only ∆113tp53 was upregulated in banprw337 mutants (Figure 4A).
evidence: Directly measured by quantitative RT-PCR.

claim: A genomic region in intron 4 of tp53 is specifically open in banprw337 mutants but not in wild-type siblings.
source: ATAC-seq revealed that a genomic region in intron 4 of tp53 is specifically open in banprw337 mutants, but not in wild-type siblings (Figure 4B, ATAC-seq).
evidence: Directly observed from ATAC-seq data.

claim: Transcription of ∆113tp53 mRNA is specifically activated in banprw337 mutants but not in wild-type siblings.
source: Consistently, transcription of the ∆113tp53 mRNA was specifically activated in banprw337 mutants, but not in wild-type siblings (Figure 4B, RNA-seq).
evidence: Directly observed from RNA-seq data.

claim: The internal promoter at intron 4 of tp53 is specifically activated in banprw337 mutants.
source: Thus, the internal promoter at intron 4 (Chen et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2005) is specifically activated in banprw337 mutants (Figure 4B).
evidence: Inferred from ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data, with reference to Chen et al., 2009 and Chen et al., 2005.

claim: The lack of Banp increases DNA replication stress and promotes accumulation of DNA damage, resulting in activation of ATR and ATM, which stabilize FL tp53, such that FL tp53 triggers ∆113tp53 transcription in banprw337 mutants.
source: These data raise the possibility that the lack of Banp increases DNA replication stress and promotes an accumulation of DNA damage, resulting in activation of ATR and ATM, which stabilize FL tp53, such that FL tp53 triggers ∆113tp53 transcription in banprw337 mutants (Figure 4G).
evidence: Proposed model based on multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The number of γ-H2AX-positive cells increases in both banprw337 mutant and banp morphant retinas.
source: The number of γ-H2AX+ cells increased in both banprw337 mutant (Figure 4C and F) and banp morphant retinas (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B), confirming an accumulation of DNA damage in the absence of Banp.
evidence: Directly quantified from γ-H2AX antibody staining.

claim: DNA damage accumulates in the absence of Banp.
source: The number of γ-H2AX+ cells increased in both banprw337 mutant (Figure 4C and F) and banp morphant retinas (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B), confirming an accumulation of DNA damage in the absence of Banp.
evidence: Inferred from the increase in γ-H2AX-positive cells.

claim: The BrdU-positive fraction is significantly higher in γ-H2AX-positive cells than in total retinal cells in banprw337 mutants.
source: The BrdU+ fraction was significantly higher in γ-H2AX+ cells than in total retinal cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F), indicating that S-phase fraction is 4.3-fold higher in DNA damaged retinal cells than in total retinal cells, in banprw337 mutants.
evidence: Directly quantified from double labeling experiments.

claim: S-phase fraction is 4.3-fold higher in DNA damaged retinal cells than in total retinal cells in banprw337 mutants.
source: The BrdU+ fraction was significantly higher in γ-H2AX+ cells than in total retinal cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F), indicating that S-phase fraction is 4.3-fold higher in DNA damaged retinal cells than in total retinal cells, in banprw337 mutants.
evidence: Calculated from the BrdU and γ-H2AX double labeling data.

claim: Replicative DNA damage is abnormally increased in retinal progenitor cells undergoing S phase in banprw337 mutants.
source: Thus, replicative DNA damage is abnormally increased in retinal progenitor cells undergoing S phase.
evidence: Inferred from the enrichment of BrdU-positive cells among γ-H2AX-positive cells.

claim: There is no significant difference in the ath5:EGFP-positive cell fraction between total retinal cells and γ-H2AX-positive retinal cells in banprw337 mutants.
source: There was no significant difference in the ath5:EGFP+ cell fraction between the total retinal cells and γ-H2AX+ retinal cells in banprw337 mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Directly quantified from double labeling experiments.

claim: There is no significant difference in the pH3-positive cell fraction between total retinal cells and γ-H2AX-positive retinal cells in banprw337 mutants.
source: There is no significant difference in the pH3+ cell fraction between the total retinal cells and γ-H2AX+ retinal cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Directly quantified from double labeling experiments.

claim: Most DNA damage is introduced in S-phase of retinal progenitor cells due to replication fork stalling in the absence of Banp.
source: Although DNA damage may occur in post-mitotic neurons and mitotic cells in banprw337 mutants, it is likely that most DNA damage is introduced in S-phase of retinal progenitor cells due to replication fork stalling in the absence of Banp.
evidence: Inferred from the enrichment of S-phase cells among DNA damaged cells.

claim: Injection of FL tp53-MO significantly reduces the number of γ-H2AX-positive cells in banprw337 mutant retinas at 48 hpf.
source: However, compared with standard-MO injection control (n=120.8 ± 60.6/section), the injection of FL tp53-MO significantly reduced the number of γ-H2AX+ cells in banprw337 mutant retinas (n=55.9 ± 15.9/section) at 48 hpf (Figure 4C and F).
evidence: Directly quantified from γ-H2AX antibody staining after morpholino injection.

claim: Injection of ∆113tp53-MO mildly reduces the number of γ-H2AX-positive cells in banprw337 mutants, but the difference is not significant.
source: Injection of ∆113tp53-MO mildly reduced the number of γ-H2AX+ cells (n=85.4 ± 15.2/section); however, the difference was not significant (Figure 4C and F).
evidence: Directly quantified from γ-H2AX antibody staining after morpholino injection.

claim: Neither tp53 nor ∆113tp53 repairs DNA damage in banprw337 mutants.
source: It is likely that neither tp53 nor ∆113tp53 repairs DNA damage in banprw337 mutants.
evidence: Inferred from the reduction of γ-H2AX-positive cells upon tp53 knockdown.

claim: Under normal conditions, Banp probably suppresses DNA replication stress upstream of tp53 by promoting recovery from stalled forks or repair of DSBs.
source: Thus, under normal conditions, Banp probably suppresses DNA replication stress upstream of tp53 by promoting recovery from stalled forks or repair of DSBs (Figure 4G).
evidence: Proposed model based on the study's findings.

claim: Inhibition of apoptosis in banprw337 mutant retinas by ∆113tp53-MO is significant but ineffective.
source: However, inhibition of apoptosis in banprw337 mutant retinas by ∆113tp53-MO was significant, but ineffective (n=58.00 ± 11.0/section) (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Directly quantified from TUNEL staining after morpholino injection.

claim: ∆113tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target genes related to cell-cycle arrest rather than apoptosis.
source: This result is consistent with previous reports proposing that ∆113tp53 preferentially activates transcription of target genes related to cell-cycle arrest rather than apoptosis (Gong et al., 2015; Gong et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from Gong et al., 2015 and Gong et al., 2020.

claim: The number of pH3-positive cells in banprw337 mutants is significantly decreased by FL tp53-MO.
source: Compared with Standard-MO injection controls (n=376.6 ± 74.8/section), the number of pH3+ cells in banprw337 mutants was significantly decreased by FL tp53-MO (n=262.4 ± 68.3/section) (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: Directly quantified from pH3 antibody staining after morpholino injection.

claim: The number of pH3-positive cells is still higher in banprw337 mutant retinas injected with FL tp53-MO than in wild-type control retinas injected with FL tp53-MO.
source: However, the number of pH3+ cells was still higher in banprw337 mutant retinas injected with FL tp53-MO than in wild-type control retinas injected with FL tp53-MO, indicating that there is a substantial tp53-independent fraction.
evidence: Directly quantified from pH3 antibody staining.

claim: There is a substantial tp53-independent fraction of mitotic cell accumulation in banprw337 mutants.
source: However, the number of pH3+ cells was still higher in banprw337 mutant retinas injected with FL tp53-MO than in wild-type control retinas injected with FL tp53-MO, indicating that there is a substantial tp53-independent fraction.
evidence: Inferred from the incomplete rescue by tp53 knockdown.

claim: Injection of ∆113tp53-MO does not significantly rescue mitotic phenotypes in banprw337 mutants.
source: Furthermore, the injection of ∆113tp53-MO did not significantly rescue mitotic phenotypes in banprw337 mutants (n=303.8 ± 46.6/section) (Figure 4C and F).
evidence: Directly quantified from pH3 antibody staining after morpholino injection.

claim: There is a tp53-independent mechanism that causes mitotic cell accumulation in banprw337 mutants.
source: These data suggest that there is a tp53-independent mechanism that causes mitotic cell accumulation in banprw337 mutants.
evidence: Inferred from the incomplete rescue of mitotic phenotypes by tp53 and ∆113tp53 knockdown.

claim: Two chromosomal segregation regulators, cenpt and ncapg, are downregulated in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: RNA-seq analysis revealed that two chromosomal segregation regulators, cenpt and ncapg, are downregulated in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf (Figure 3B).
evidence: Directly observed from RNA-seq data.

claim: Cenpt and Ncapg are essential for chromatin segregation.
source: Cenpt and Ncapg are essential for chromatin segregation (Hung et al., 2017; Seipold et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from Hung et al., 2017; Seipold et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: cenpt and ncapg mRNAs are expressed in retinal progenitor cells.
source: Using in situ hybridization, we confirmed that their mRNAs are expressed in retinal progenitor cells and that expression of both mRNAs is markedly decreased in banp mutants at 48 hpf (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: Expression of cenpt and ncapg mRNAs is markedly decreased in banp mutants at 48 hpf.
source: Using in situ hybridization, we confirmed that their mRNAs are expressed in retinal progenitor cells and that expression of both mRNAs is markedly decreased in banp mutants at 48 hpf (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: Quantitative RT-PCR confirms downregulation of cenpt and ncapg in banprw337 mutants and banp morphants.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR also confirmed their downregulation in banprw337 mutants and banp morphants (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: Directly measured by quantitative RT-PCR.

claim: Chromatin accessibility is decreased near the transcription start site of both cenpt and ncapg genes in banprw337 mutants.
source: Furthermore, ATAC-seq revealed that chromatin accessibility is decreased near the transcription start site (TSS) of both genes in banprw337 mutants, leading to reduction of transcription activity (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: Directly observed from ATAC-seq data.

claim: Banp is required for transcriptional activation of cenpt and ncapg genes.
source: Thus, Banp is required for transcriptional activation of cenpt and ncapg genes.
evidence: Inferred from the decreased chromatin accessibility and mRNA expression in banp mutants.

claim: Two independent chip-sequencing studies using BANP antibody revealed a specific binding site within 100 bp of the TSS of Cenpt and Ncapg genes in mice and humans.
source: Interestingly, two independent chip-sequencing studies using BANP antibody revealed a specific binding site within 100 bp of the TSS of Cenpt and Ncapg genes in mice and humans (Grand et al., 2021; Mathai et al., 2016), suggesting that the requirement for Banp in cenpt and ncapg transcription is conserved in zebrafish, mice, and humans.
evidence: Cited from Grand et al., 2021 and Mathai et al., 2016.

claim: The requirement for Banp in cenpt and ncapg transcription is conserved in zebrafish, mice, and humans.
source: Interestingly, two independent chip-sequencing studies using BANP antibody revealed a specific binding site within 100 bp of the TSS of Cenpt and Ncapg genes in mice and humans (Grand et al., 2021; Mathai et al., 2016), suggesting that the requirement for Banp in cenpt and ncapg transcription is conserved in zebrafish, mice, and humans.
evidence: Inferred from the conservation of BANP binding sites across species.

claim: The duration of mitosis from prophase to telophase is significantly longer in banp morphants than in control embryos.
source: The duration from prophase to telophase was 49.2±17.0 min and significantly longer in banp morphants (Figure 5F).
evidence: Directly measured from live imaging experiments.

claim: Chromosomal segregation is abnormal during mitosis in the absence of Banp.
source: Thus, chromosomal segregation is abnormal during mitosis in the absence of Banp.
evidence: Inferred from live imaging showing prolonged and irregular mitosis.

claim: In banprw337 mutants, mitotic spindles are irregularly attached to less condensed and misaligned chromosomes.
source: In banprw337 mutants, mitotic spindles are irregularly attached to less condensed and misaligned chromosomes (Figure 5G).
evidence: Directly observed through immunofluorescence microscopy.

claim: The percentage of cells with abnormal mitosis is significantly higher in banprw337 mutant retinas than in wild-type siblings.
source: The percentage of cells with abnormal mitosis was significantly higher in banprw337 mutant retinas than those of wild-type siblings (Figure 5H).
evidence: Directly quantified from immunofluorescence microscopy.

claim: The interaction between chromosomes and mitotic spindles is compromised in the absence of Banp, probably due to kinetochore attachment defects caused by lack of Cenpt and Ncapg.
source: These data suggest that the interaction between chromosomes and mitotic spindles is compromised in the absence of Banp, probably due to kinetochore attachment defects caused by lack of Cenpt and Ncapg.
evidence: Inferred from the abnormal spindle attachment and known functions of Cenpt and Ncapg.

claim: Banp regulates chromosomal segregation during mitosis.
source: Thus, Banp regulates chromosomal segregation during mitosis.
evidence: Summarized from live imaging and immunofluorescence data.

claim: BANP binds to the nucleotide sequence TCTCGCGAGA, called the 'Banp motif'.
source: Recently, it was reported that BANP binds to the nucleotide sequence TCTCGCGAGA, called the 'Banp motif' and regulates transcription of essential metabolic genes in humans and mice (Grand et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from Grand et al., 2021.

claim: BANP regulates transcription of essential metabolic genes in humans and mice.
source: Recently, it was reported that BANP binds to the nucleotide sequence TCTCGCGAGA, called the 'Banp motif' and regulates transcription of essential metabolic genes in humans and mice (Grand et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from Grand et al., 2021.

claim: TCTCGCGAGA is the most enriched motif in the closed chromatin region of banprw337 mutants.
source: Consistent with a previous report on human and mouse BANP (Grand et al., 2021), our analysis revealed that TCTCGCGAGA, is the most enriched motif in the closed chromatin region of banprw337 mutants (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Directly determined from HOMER motif analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: Among 81 downregulated genes in banprw337 mutants, 31 genes have the Banp motif near their TSSs.
source: Indeed, among 81 down-regulated genes in banprw337 mutants (Figure 3A), we identified the Banp motif near TSS of 31 genes (Figure 6B and C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Directly determined from motif scanning of downregulated genes.

claim: The Banp motif is not found among 258 upregulated genes in banprw337 mutants.
source: However, we could not find the Banp motif among 258 upregulated genes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Directly determined from motif scanning of upregulated genes.

claim: Banp is a transcription activator of multiple gene targets containing Banp motifs.
source: These data suggest that Banp is a transcription activator of multiple gene targets containing Banp motifs.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of Banp motifs in downregulated but not upregulated genes.

claim: Among the transcription targets of Banp that are downregulated in banprw337 mutants, 26 percent are involved in regulating cell cycle.
source: Among the transcription targets of Banp that are downregulated in banprw337 mutants, 26 percent were involved in regulating cell cycle (Figure 6D), including ncapg (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), cenpt (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), and wrnip1 (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Directly determined from gene ontology analysis.

claim: ncapg, cenpt, and wrnip1 are among the cell cycle regulators that are direct targets of Banp.
source: Among the transcription targets of Banp that are downregulated in banprw337 mutants, 26 percent were involved in regulating cell cycle (Figure 6D), including ncapg (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), cenpt (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), and wrnip1 (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Directly identified from RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and motif analysis.

claim: wrnip1 protects stalled replication forks from MRE11-mediated degradation and promotes fork restart after replication stress.
source: In addition, wrnip1 is interesting, because it protects stalled replication forks from MRE11-mediated degradation and promotes fork restart after replication stress (Leuzzi et al., 2016a; Leuzzi et al., 2016b).
evidence: Cited from Leuzzi et al., 2016a and Leuzzi et al., 2016b.

claim: wrnip1 mRNA is normally expressed in retinal progenitor cells in zebrafish.
source: We confirmed that wrnip1 mRNA is normally expressed in retinal progenitor cells in zebrafish and that its expression is reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: wrnip1 mRNA expression is reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf.
source: We confirmed that wrnip1 mRNA is normally expressed in retinal progenitor cells in zebrafish and that its expression is reduced in banprw337 mutants at 48 hpf (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Directly observed through in situ hybridization.

claim: Quantitative RT-PCR reveals a significant reduction of wrnip1 mRNA expression in both banp mutants and morphants.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR analysis revealed a significant reduction of wrnip1 mRNA expression in both banp mutants and morphants (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Directly measured by quantitative RT-PCR.

claim: Banp is required to maintain wrnip1 mRNA expression in retinal progenitor cells in zebrafish.
source: These data suggest that Banp is required to maintain wrnip1 mRNA expression in retinal progenitor cells in zebrafish.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced wrnip1 expression in banp mutants and morphants.

claim: Loss of wrnip1 is expected to cause genomic instability due to excessive fork degradation.
source: Loss of wrnip1 is expected to cause genomic instability due to excessive fork degradation (Leuzzi et al., 2016b).
evidence: Cited from Leuzzi et al., 2016b.

claim: The reduction of wrnip1 mRNA expression may explain the significant accumulation of γ-H2AX-positive retinal cells in banprw337 mutants.
source: So, the reduction of wrnip1 mRNA expression may explain the significant accumulation of γ-H2AX+ retinal cells in banprw337 mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Speculated based on the known function of wrnip1 and the observed phenotypes.

claim: Banp regulates transcription of multiple target genes, including cell-cycle regulators.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Banp regulates transcription of multiple target genes, including these cell-cycle regulators.
evidence: Summarized from RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and motif analysis.

claim: During S phase, Banp suppresses DNA replication stress by activating transcription of wrnip1.
source: During S phase, Banp suppresses DNA replication stress by activating transcription of a DNA replication stress regulator, wrnip1, and promotes DNA damage repair in concert with tp53-mediated DNA damage response.
evidence: Proposed model based on the study's findings.

claim: Banp promotes DNA damage repair in concert with tp53-mediated DNA damage response.
source: During S phase, Banp suppresses DNA replication stress by activating transcription of a DNA replication stress regulator, wrnip1, and promotes DNA damage repair in concert with tp53-mediated DNA damage response.
evidence: Proposed model based on the study's findings.

claim: In M phase, Banp promotes mitosis by activating transcription of cenpt and ncapg.
source: In M phase, Banp promotes mitosis by activating transcription of two chromosome segregation regulators, cenpt and ncapg, most likely via their Banp motifs.
evidence: Proposed model based on the study's findings.

claim: Banp regulates progression in S phase and M phase through transcriptional control of distinct sets of cell-cycle regulators.
source: Thus, Banp regulates progression in S phase and M phase through transcriptional control of distinct sets of cell-cycle regulators.
evidence: Summarized from the study's findings.

claim: In banp mutants, stalled DNA replication and subsequent DSBs are accumulated in S phase, resulting in increased apoptosis.
source: In banp mutants, stalled DNA replication and subsequent DSBs are accumulated in S phase, resulting in increase in apoptosis.
evidence: Summarized from the study's findings.

claim: In M phase, banp mutants show chromosome segregation defects, which prolong mitosis but eventually complete it.
source: In M phase, banp mutants show chromosome segregation defects, which prolongs mitosis but eventually complete it.
evidence: Directly observed from live imaging experiments.

claim: DNA damage mostly induced in S phase is likely inherited through mitosis by daughter cells in banp mutants.
source: So, DNA damage mostly induced in S phase is likely to be inherited through mitosis by daughter cells, which reenter the cell-cycle or become post-mitotic neurons.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that mitosis completes despite DNA damage.

claim: Neurons with a high level of DNA damage may undergo apoptosis in banp mutants.
source: Neurons with a high level of DNA damage may undergo apoptosis.
evidence: Speculated based on the observed apoptosis patterns.

claim: S phase defects and M phase defects influence each other along cell-cycle progression of retinal progenitor cells in the absence of Banp.
source: Thus, S phase defects and M phase defects influence each other along cell-cycle progression of retinal progenitor cells in the absence of Banp (Figure 7B).
evidence: Proposed model based on the study's findings.
